question: Is more acquisition the right next move?

sources.title: Three-week delivery ledger
sources.excerpt: Weeks ending Sep 3, 10, 17: orders 20, 30, 40; late orders 1, 6, 14; support tickets 2, 7, 15. Same service and definition of late. Reviewer receives totals only, not customer records.
omitted: Names and identifiers not needed for the review are not included.

sources.title: Redacted workflow excerpt
sources.excerpt: Each order requires human QA before release. QA has one owner. Demand doubled; QA time allocation stayed at 10 hours per week. Queue-age measurements were not recorded.
omitted: Names and identifiers not needed for the review are not included.

sources.title: Founder counter-explanation
sources.excerpt: The last week included a new integration used on 12 orders. I think new customers are harder to serve. No breakdown of lateness by integration or customer group is available.
omitted: Names and identifiers not needed for the review are not included.

product_service.statement: The supplied three-week totals show orders rising from 20 to 40 while late orders rise from 1 to 14. A changed integration and limited QA time are competing explanations, not established causes.

customer.statement: Support-ticket totals rise with order volume; the packet does not establish which customers experienced delays or whether retention changed.

skills.statement: The workflow excerpt names one QA owner with unchanged weekly allocation. It does not establish skill quality or prove that hiring is necessary.

interactions.statement: MOCK illustration: acquisition growth may increase pressure on delivery and support, but queue ages and integration-specific lateness are missing.

unknowns: Cash collection, margin, refunds and retention effects are not supplied.
Queue age by stage and lateness by integration or complexity are unknown.
No single bottleneck or recurring system pattern is established by this mock output.

alternatives.explanation: The new integration may explain some late orders; alternatively QA capacity or order complexity may have changed. These are untested hypotheses.

nextTest.question: Are late orders concentrated in the new-integration group?
nextTest.action: Founder: within one business day, spend at most 30 minutes producing only a redacted aggregate late/total split for the 12 new-integration orders versus the remaining orders. No names, outreach or spend. Stop if the same lateness definition or scope cannot be confirmed.
nextTest.successSignal: A materially higher late proportion in the integration group supports prioritizing that explanation; a similar proportion weakens it and leaves QA/complexity uncertain.

omissions: Authored provider-MOCK PS02 illustration for request/response plumbing only; no model called and no method-quality evaluation.
Only the existing PS02 fictional input was used. Evaluator-only expectations are not sent to the reviewer.
